payload.title: The new policy key anchor_tp_pairs_per_tool_per_cycle is converted with int() in the cycle under an except GovernanceError, and judgment_pipeline_policy merges operator override values with no type check, so a null or non-numeric override raises TypeError or ValueError out of the judgment pipeline phase instead of a named blocked step.
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cycle.py:2216-2224 (int(pipeline_policy[...]) inside a try that catches GovernanceError only)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:1267-1268 (the dispatcher's own default read converts the same value with int())
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/genesis_policy.py:233-251 (judgment_pipeline_policy copies override sub-keys with no validation)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/genesis_policy.py:363-385 (executor_policy validates and raises GovernanceError naming the field)
payload.rule_violated: Policy accessors are parsed strictly and refuse a bad value by name (executor_policy, circuit_breaker_policy); a value the accessor lets through must not be able to crash the phase that reads it.
payload.notes: A repo override {"judgment_pipeline": {"anchor_tp_pairs_per_tool_per_cycle": null}} (or "five") reaches int(None) at cycle.py:2220: a TypeError, not a GovernanceError, so the per-tool containment does not catch it and the judgment pipeline phase raises for every tool of the cycle instead of recording a blocked 'anchoring' step. The override file is operator-owned, so the trigger is an operator typo, but it fails the whole phase every cycle until fixed. Close condition: Validate anchor_tp_pairs_per_tool_per_cycle (and the other judgment_pipeline keys) in judgment_pipeline_policy as a non-negative int and raise GovernanceError naming the key; test that null, a string and -1 overrides each raise GovernanceError and that the cycle records a blocked anchoring step. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
